doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Interview embarrassments and the Internet
summary: Lack of research is his embarrassment, and he finds the Internet a seductive time sink.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Speaking of unpleasant, did you ever have an interview that just left you feeling embarrassed or like you really put your foot in it somehow?

I’ll have to think about that. I think the things that embarrass me is where I find or where it appears early on that I should have done a hell of a lot more research. I think that is embarrassing. You know when a guys says, “Well don’t you know about my recordings?” Ah. That’s a tricky moment. And that’s perhaps where one’s been a little bit

too quick to fix the interview, on a sort of sense of saying well this guy won’t be here more than another day, I must do it now. And you can quite often regret that you didn’t have that time. And I know I’ve not been as professional as I should have been.
Has the Internet and all the explosion of information helped you?

Yeah I use it occasionally. I find it’s too seductive. It can take up too much time. You know if you’re not careful you can kind of wile away a couple of hours and if you’re really truthful the value you’ve had from that time may not have been that great. So it’s just, it’s a background tool. But that’s as far as it goes I think.
